column1: # How a legal form is written in a company's name (curated 2026-11-11 for Milestone 5), where the
# form's abbreviation is missing, wrong for a name, or not how names are written. Applied by
# prepare_forms.py after form_overrides.tsv, to ISO, pseudo and template forms alike.
# match: an ISO 20275 code, a form key (legal_forms.tsv), or /regex/ on the form's name, Latin
# name or abbreviation (case-insensitive). abbreviation, latin_abbreviation: set the form's own
# ("-" clears it). in_name: alternatives separated by "|", one picked evenly; "{name}" marks
# where the rest of the name goes; "-" is the name without the form; text without "{name}" is
# placed as the language's style says (suffix, prefix, or either). Empty: the abbreviation, placed
# by the style, and nothing for a form without one. An in_name in another script than the name's
# language is not used: the Latin abbreviation is placed instead.
# Sources: the company laws' rules on firm names (e.g. Germany HGB s. 19, France Code de commerce
# R123-238 and the 2022 "EI" rule, Japan Companies Act art. 6, Russia Civil Code art. 1473, Viet
# Nam Enterprise Law 2020 art. 38, Thailand Civil and Commercial Code s. 1015 and 1100), and how
# registered names are written in the registers (Companies House, SIRENE, Enhetsregisteret).
